questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The forelimbs of whales, bats, cheetahs and humans perform very different functions. However, all of them are built of humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. This pattern is an outcome of
options: Convergent evolution
Divergent evolution
Analogy produced by a similar habitat
Inheritance of acquired characters
questions.explanation:
Whale, bat, cheetah and human forelimbs share the same bones: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
The same ancestral structure has been modified in different directions for swimming, flying, running and grasping. This is divergent evolution, and it produces homologous organs.
Convergent evolution (and analogy from a similar habitat) works the other way: different structures come to perform the same function. Inheritance of acquired characters is Lamarck's discarded idea.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Consider two pairs of structures used for flight: (P) wing of a bird and wing of a bat; (Q) wing of a bird and wing of a butterfly. Considered as anatomical structures, how should P and Q be classified?
options: P is homologous, Q is analogous
P is analogous, Q is homologous
Both P and Q are analogous because all of them are used for flight
Both P and Q are homologous because all of them are wings
questions.explanation:
P: Bird and bat wings are both modified vertebrate forelimbs. They share the same bone plan (humerus, radius-ulna, carpals, phalanges) and a common origin, so as forelimbs they are homologous.
Q: The butterfly wing is an outgrowth of the insect body wall with no such bone plan. It is only functionally similar to a bird wing, so the pair is analogous.
Option (3) is the trap: it classifies by function (flight) instead of by anatomy and origin.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1938, a fish caught off South Africa turned out to belong to a group thought to be extinct. To which group did this fish, the Coelacanth, belong?
options: Jawless fish
Lobefins
Cartilaginous fish
Fish-like reptiles
questions.explanation:
Lobefins are fish with stout, strong fins that could move between land and water. They gave rise to the first amphibians.
Lobefins were thought to be extinct until a Coelacanth was caught off South Africa in 1938.
It is not jawless or cartilaginous.
It is not a fish-like reptile, which is what Ichthyosaurs were.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Lichens can be used as indicators of industrial pollution because they:
options: grow faster in areas with heavy industrial smoke
turn dark in colour when exposed to soot
do not grow in polluted areas
absorb soot and keep tree trunks white
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: lichens are very sensitive to pollutants such as $SO_2$ and soot, so they do not grow in polluted areas.
So where lichens are absent, the air is polluted. Their absence works as a natural pollution indicator.
In industrial England, lichens disappeared from tree trunks. Soot then darkened the bare bark.
Option (4) is tempting but wrong. Lichens do not absorb soot to keep trunks white. They simply disappear under pollution.
Options (1) and (2) are also wrong. Lichens neither thrive in smoke nor change colour.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I (event) with List-II (approximate time) according to NCERT.
List-I
A. Appearance of first cellular forms of life
B. Invertebrates formed and active
C. Seaweeds and a few plants existed
D. Sudden disappearance of dinosaurs
List-II
I. About 320 mya
II. About 65 mya
III. About 2000 mya
IV. About 500 mya
options: A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-IV, C-III, D-II
questions.explanation:
A: The first cellular forms of life appeared about 2000 mya, so A–III.
B: Invertebrates were formed and active by about 500 mya, so B–IV.
C: Seaweeds and a few plants existed around 320 mya, so C–I.
D: Dinosaurs disappeared suddenly about 65 mya, so D–II.
Only option (1) gives A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about adaptive radiation in Australia is INCORRECT?
options: A number of different marsupials evolved from an ancestral stock within the Australian continent
Placental mammals in Australia also show adaptive radiation into varieties resembling corresponding marsupials
The resemblance of the Tasmanian wolf to the placental wolf shows that these two share a more recent common ancestor with each other than with other marsupials
Occurrence of more than one adaptive radiation in an isolated geographical area can be described as convergent evolution
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: different Australian marsupials evolved from an ancestral stock within the continent.
(2) Correct: Australian placental mammals also radiated, giving varieties that each resemble a corresponding marsupial.
(3) Incorrect: the Tasmanian wolf is a marsupial, so it shares a more recent ancestor with other marsupials than with the placental wolf. Their likeness comes from similar habitats, not close kinship.
(4) Correct: more than one adaptive radiation in an isolated area is called convergent evolution.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Wings of a butterfly and wings of a bird are analogous structures.
Reason (R): Wings of a butterfly and a bird are anatomically similar structures that perform different functions.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Butterfly and bird wings are analogous: they differ in origin and anatomy but perform the same function, flight.
R is false. The wings are not anatomically similar, and they do not perform different functions. R actually describes neither homology nor analogy correctly.
So A is true but R is false.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which hominin, with a brain size of about 1400 cc, used hides to protect its body and buried its dead?
options: Homo habilis
Homo erectus
Australopithecus
Neanderthal man
questions.explanation:
Neanderthal man had a brain size of about 1400 cc.
It lived in the near east and central Asia between 1,00,000 and 40,000 years ago.
It used hides to protect its body and buried its dead.
Homo erectus is the tempting wrong choice, but its brain was only about 900 cc.
Homo habilis (650–800 cc) and Australopithecus had even smaller brains.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Pouched mammals of Australia survived, whereas many South American mammals resembling horse, hippopotamus and bear did not.
Reason (R): Continental drift kept Australian marsupials free from competition with other mammals, while the joining of South and North America exposed South American mammals to North American fauna.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. NCERT notes that Australian marsupials survived. Many South American mammals resembling horse, hippopotamus and bear disappeared.
R is true. Continental drift kept Australia isolated, so its marsupials faced no competition from other mammals.
When South America joined North America, its mammals were overridden by North American fauna.
R explains both outcomes, so it is the correct explanation of A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Lamarck proposed that evolution of life forms was driven by use and disuse of organs, citing giraffes that elongated their necks while foraging on tall trees.
Statement II: Lamarck's idea of inheritance of such acquired characters is the currently accepted explanation for the long neck of giraffes.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Lamarck said evolution was driven by use and disuse of organs. His example was giraffes stretching their necks to reach leaves on tall trees and passing the longer neck to their offspring.
Statement II is incorrect. NCERT states that nobody believes this conjecture any more. The inheritance of acquired characters is not the accepted explanation.
The accepted view is natural selection acting on heritable variation, as proposed by Darwin.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Darwin's finches
(B) Tasmanian wolf and placental wolf
(C) Forelimbs of whale and bat
(D) Wings of butterfly and bird
List-II
(i) Similarity between members of two separate radiations in the same isolated continent
(ii) Radiation from a seed-eating ancestral form
(iii) Different structures of an insect and a vertebrate performing the same function
(iv) Same bone pattern modified for different functions in mammals
options: A-ii, B-i, C-iv, D-iii
A-i, B-ii, C-iii, D-iv
A-ii, B-iv, C-i, D-iii
A-iv, B-i, C-ii, D-iii
questions.explanation:
(A) Darwin's finches radiated from a seed-eating ancestral form into insectivorous and other varieties, so A-ii.
(B) The Tasmanian wolf (marsupial) resembles the placental wolf. These are members of two separate radiations in isolated Australia, so B-i.
(C) Whale flipper and bat wing share the same mammalian forelimb bone pattern modified for different functions. They are homologous, so C-iv.
(D) Butterfly and bird wings are different structures of an insect and a vertebrate doing the same job. They are analogous, so D-iii.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are examples of homology?
(i) Hearts of different vertebrates
(ii) Brains of different vertebrates
(iii) Flippers of penguins and dolphins
(iv) Eye of octopus and eye of mammals
(v) Forelimbs of cheetah and human
(vi) Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
(vii) Wings of butterfly and birds
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.explanation:
Homologous organs share a common origin but may differ in function.
Homologous: (i) vertebrate hearts, (ii) vertebrate brains, (v) cheetah and human forelimbs, (vi) Bougainvillea thorn and Cucurbita tendril.
Analogous (same function, different origin): (iii) penguin and dolphin flippers, (iv) octopus and mammal eyes, (vii) butterfly and bird wings.
That gives four examples of homology.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A population is in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium for a gene with two alleles. In this population, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype. What percentage of the population is heterozygous?
questions.explanation:
Given: recessive phenotype (aa) = 16%, so $q^2 = 0.16$.
Formula: $p + q = 1$; heterozygote frequency $= 2pq$.
Substituting: $q = \sqrt{0.16} = 0.4$, so $p = 0.6$. Then $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$.
So heterozygotes = 48%. Choosing 24% means forgetting the factor 2.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following was NOT among the gases released from the molten mass that covered the surface of the early earth?
options: Water vapour
Methane
Ammonia
Free molecular oxygen
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the molten mass on the early earth released water vapour, methane, carbon dioxide and ammonia.
Free oxygen was not among these gases. It appeared only later, when UV rays split water.
So water vapour, methane and ammonia were all released, and free O$_2$ was not.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Embryos of all vertebrates, including humans, develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head. In which of the following groups is this structure a functional organ in the adult?
options: Amphibians
Fish
Reptiles
Mammals
questions.explanation:
All vertebrate embryos develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head.
NCERT states that these slits become a functional organ only in adult fish. They are not found in any other adult vertebrate.
Amphibians are tempting because their larvae breathe through gills. However, adult amphibians lack functional gill slits.
Reptiles and mammals also lose the slits during development.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and human do different jobs. Yet all of them have humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges. What does this pattern show?
options: Analogy resulting from convergent evolution
Homology resulting from divergent evolution
Homology resulting from convergent evolution
Analogy resulting from divergent evolution
questions.explanation:
The forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and human do different jobs.
Yet they share the same basic bone plan: humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals and phalanges.
Same structure with different functions defines homologous organs. They arise when a common ancestral plan is modified in different directions, which is divergent evolution.
Analogy (options 1 and 4) means similar function with different structure, which is not the case here. Convergent evolution produces analogy, not homology.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
(A) Charles Darwin
(B) Alfred Wallace
(C) Jean-Baptiste Lamarck
(D) Thomas Malthus
List-II
(I) Work on populations that possibly influenced the idea of natural selection
(II) Observations made during the voyage of H.M.S. Beagle
(III) Evolution driven by use and disuse of organs
(IV) Independent, similar conclusions from work in the Malay Archipelago
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-IV, C-I, D-III
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
A, Darwin: he drew his conclusions from observations made during the voyage of H.M.S. Beagle (II).
B, Wallace: he worked in the Malay Archipelago and reached similar conclusions independently (IV).
C, Lamarck: he proposed evolution driven by use and disuse of organs (III).
D, Malthus: his work on populations possibly influenced the idea of natural selection (I).
So the matching is A-II, B-IV, C-III, D-I. The common trap is swapping Darwin and Wallace.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are examples of analogous structures?
(i) Eye of octopus and eye of mammals
(ii) Flippers of penguins and flippers of dolphins
(iii) Sweet potato and potato
(iv) Forelimbs of whale and forelimbs of bat
(v) Hearts of different vertebrates
(vi) Wings of butterfly and wings of birds
options: Two
Three
Four
Five
questions.explanation:
Analogous structures do similar jobs but have different origins. Homologous structures share an origin but may do different jobs.
(i) Octopus and mammal eyes: analogous. (ii) Penguin and dolphin flippers: analogous. (iii) Sweet potato (modified root) and potato (modified stem): analogous.
(iv) Whale and bat forelimbs: homologous, with the same bone pattern. (v) Vertebrate hearts: homologous.
(vi) Butterfly wings (cuticle) and bird wings (forelimb): analogous.
So four pairs are analogous.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to NCERT, fossils are best described as:
options: Living organisms that have remained unchanged for millions of years
Remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks
Imprints of soft tissues formed only in volcanic lava
Organic molecules formed by electric discharge in a primitive atmosphere
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: fossils are remains of hard parts of life-forms found in rocks.
Rocks form sediments, and different strata hold different life-forms, so fossils record extinct organisms.
Option (4) is tempting but wrong. It describes the organic molecules formed in Miller's electric-discharge experiment.
Option (1) describes 'living fossils', which are living organisms, not fossils.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries proposed that mutations, rather than small heritable variations, cause evolution. Which option correctly pairs the plant he studied with the term he used for speciation by a single large mutational step?
options: Evening primrose – saltation
Garden pea – saltation
Evening primrose – genetic drift
Garden pea – founder effect
questions.explanation:
Hugo deVries based his mutation theory on his work with evening primrose (Oenothera).
He used the term saltation for speciation by a single, large, sudden mutational step.
Garden pea was Mendel's plant, so (2) and (4) fail.
Genetic drift and founder effect are chance changes in allele frequency, not deVries' term for mutational speciation.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The bones of forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and man are similar in structure, because:
options: one organism has given rise to another
they share a common ancestor
they perform the same function
they have biochemical similarities
questions.explanation:
Key fact: The forelimbs of whale, bat, cheetah and man have the same basic bone pattern (humerus, radius, ulna, carpals, metacarpals, phalanges) but perform different functions: swimming, flying, running and grasping.
Such organs are homologous. They are inherited from a common ancestor and modified by divergent evolution.
Option (3) fails because these limbs perform different functions. Similar function with different structure would make them analogous organs.
Option (1) is wrong because none of these animals gave rise to another.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q5)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The NCERT family tree of dinosaurs (Figure 6.2) links these extinct reptiles to which living modern-day counterparts?
options: Crocodiles and birds
Frogs and salamanders
Whales and dolphins
Sharks and bony fishes
questions.explanation:
NCERT Figure 6.2 shows a family tree of dinosaurs.
The tree links these extinct reptiles to their living modern-day counterparts, crocodiles and birds.
Dinosaurs themselves are known only from fossils, so they are an example of extinct organisms.
Frogs and salamanders, whales and dolphins, and sharks and bony fishes do not appear as dinosaur descendants in the figure.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
In a large population in Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype (aa). Consider the following statements:
(i) The frequency of allele A is 0.6.
(ii) 48% of the individuals are heterozygous (Aa).
(iii) The frequency of homozygous dominant (AA) individuals is 0.36.
(iv) Repeated migration of individuals from a different population into this one would leave its allele frequencies unchanged.
How many of the above statements are correct?
options: One
Two
Three
Four
questions.explanation:
Given: $q^2 = 0.16$, so $q = 0.4$ and $p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$.
(i) Correct: the frequency of allele A is $p = 0.6$.
(ii) Correct: $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4 = 0.48$, so 48% are heterozygous.
(iii) Correct: $p^2 = 0.6^2 = 0.36$.
(iv) Incorrect: repeated migration causes gene flow, which adds or removes alleles. This changes allele frequencies and disturbs the equilibrium.
So three statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In 1938, a fish that was believed to be extinct was caught off the coast of a particular country and identified as a Coelacanth. Which country was it?
options: Australia
South Africa
Brazil
Madagascar
questions.explanation:
NCERT notes that in 1938 a fish caught in South Africa turned out to be a Coelacanth. It is a lobefin that had been thought to be extinct.
Australia is tempting because the chapter mentions it for adaptive radiation of marsupials, not for the Coelacanth.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Animal husbandry and plant breeding programmes are the examples of:
options: reverse evolution
artificial selection
mutation
natural selection
questions.explanation:
Key fact: In animal husbandry and plant breeding, humans choose which individuals with desired traits are allowed to reproduce.
Because humans, not nature, do the selecting, this is artificial selection. Darwin used it as an analogy for natural selection.
Natural selection is tempting, but in it the environment determines survival and reproduction without human choice.
Mutation is a source of variation, not a selection process, and 'reverse evolution' is not the right term here.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A population of 400 diploid plants contains 200 AA, 120 Aa and 80 aa individuals. Calculate the frequency of allele a from these counts. If a population of the same size and the same allele frequencies were in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, how many aa individuals would be expected?
questions.explanation:
Given: 400 plants, so there are 800 alleles. The counts are AA = 200, Aa = 120, aa = 80.
Formula: $q = \frac{\text{Aa} + 2(\text{aa})}{2N}$; expected aa $= q^2 N$.
Substituting: $q = \frac{120 + 160}{800} = 0.35$. Then $q^2 = 0.1225$, and $0.1225 \times 400 = 49$.
So 49 aa plants are expected. The observed 80 is not equal to 49, so this population is not in equilibrium.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about industrial melanism in England is INCORRECT?
options: After industrialisation, soot darkened tree trunks, so white-winged moths were easily spotted by predators.
In rural areas where industrialisation did not occur, the count of melanic moths stayed low.
After industrialisation, white-winged moths were completely wiped out from the industrial areas.
Moths that could camouflage against the background of the tree bark survived better.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: soot-covered dark trunks made white moths easy for predators to spot.
(2) Correct: in rural areas without industrialisation, the count of melanic moths stayed low.
(3) Incorrect: white-winged moths were not completely wiped out. Only the ratio of white to dark moths was reversed, and NCERT stresses that no variant is completely eliminated.
(4) Correct: moths camouflaged against the bark escaped predators and survived better.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements are correct?
(i) The sum total of all allelic frequencies of a gene in a population is 1.
(ii) $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ is the binomial expansion of $(p+q)^2$.
(iii) In disruptive selection, more individuals acquire the mean character value.
(iv) Gene flow occurs when gene migration happens multiple times.
(v) The direction of difference between measured and expected allele frequencies indicates the extent of evolutionary change.
(vi) Darwin built his theory on Mendel's inheritable factors to explain the origin of variation.
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: the allele frequencies of a gene sum to 1.
(ii) Correct: $(p+q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$.
(iii) Incorrect: favouring the mean is stabilising selection. Disruptive selection favours both extremes.
(iv) Correct: gene migration that happens many times is gene flow.
(v) Correct: per NCERT, the difference (direction) between measured and expected values indicates the extent of evolutionary change.
(vi) Incorrect: Darwin ignored Mendel's factors or kept silent about them.
Four statements are correct.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about Pasteur's 'killed yeast' experiment is INCORRECT?
options: In pre-sterilised flasks, no life arose from the killed yeast.
In a flask open to air, new living organisms appeared on the killed yeast.
The experiment dismissed the theory of spontaneous generation.
The experiment explained how the first life form originated on earth.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: no life arose from killed yeast in the pre-sterilised flasks.
(2) Correct: new organisms appeared in the flask open to air.
(3) Correct: the result dismissed spontaneous generation.
(4) Incorrect: Pasteur only showed that life comes from pre-existing life. He did not explain how the very first life form originated; the Oparin–Haldane hypothesis later addressed that.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Suppose strict pollution control in an industrial area of England stops soot deposition. Over many years, whitish lichens grow back on the tree trunks. Based on NCERT's explanation of industrial melanism, what is the most likely outcome in the moth population?
options: Melanic moths will be completely eliminated within one generation
The proportion of white-winged moths will rise again, while melanic moths decline but are not completely wiped out
Melanic moths will turn white because the cleaner environment induces the colour change
The moth proportions will stay as they are, because selection cannot reverse a change once it has occurred
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: moths survive better when their wing colour matches the tree bark, because predators then cannot spot them easily.
On clean, lichen-covered pale trunks, white-winged moths are camouflaged again. Melanic moths stand out and are eaten more often.
So selection again favours white moths and their proportion rises. Melanic moths decline but are not wiped out, since NCERT stresses that no variant is completely eliminated.
(1) fails because elimination in one generation is impossible. (3) is Lamarckian: colour is inherited, not induced. (4) is wrong because selection depends on the current environment and can reverse direction.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph shows the frequency distribution of a trait in a population before and after natural selection. After selection, individuals with the mean value become fewer, and two peaks appear at both ends of the curve. This pattern represents:
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Genetic drift
questions.explanation:
In disruptive selection, the peripheral values at both ends of the curve are favoured. Individuals near the mean decline, so two peaks appear.
The described pattern matches this exactly.
Stabilising selection favours the mean and narrows a single peak.
Directional selection shifts the whole curve toward one end only.
Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequency, not selection producing two peaks.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: About 15 million years ago, two primates, Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus, existed. Which statement correctly compares them?
options: Dryopithecus was more man-like, while Ramapithecus was more ape-like
Ramapithecus was more man-like, while Dryopithecus was more ape-like
Both were hairless and walked fully upright
Both had a brain capacity of about 900 cc
questions.explanation:
Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed about 15 mya.
NCERT states that Ramapithecus was more man-like, while Dryopithecus was more ape-like. Option (1) reverses this.
Both were hairy and walked like gorillas and chimpanzees, so option (3) is wrong.
A brain capacity of about 900 cc belongs to Homo erectus, so option (4) is wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph plots the number of individuals against the value of a trait. Before selection, the population shows a single bell-shaped curve with its peak at the mean. After many generations of selection, the curve has two peaks, one at each end of the original distribution, with fewer individuals near the mean. Which type of natural selection does this represent?
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Artificial selection
questions.explanation:
The original curve has one peak, with most individuals near the mean value.
After selection there are two peaks at the extremes and few individuals near the mean. So the extreme (peripheral) phenotypes are favoured and the mean is selected against. This is disruptive selection.
Stabilising selection would make the single central peak taller and narrower.
Directional selection would shift the single peak toward one end.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: According to Darwin, the variations that drive evolution are small and directional, and evolution is gradual.
Statement II: Hugo deVries believed that the minor heritable variations described by Darwin, rather than mutations, cause evolution.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Darwin saw variations as small and directional, and evolution as gradual.
Statement II is incorrect. deVries, working on evening primrose, argued that mutations cause evolution, not Darwin's minor variations. He described mutations as large, sudden, random and directionless, which he called saltation.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Humans have produced many breeds of dogs through intensive breeding. How is this used as an argument in support of evolution?
options: Each dog breed has become a separate species, proving that speciation is rapid
It shows that characters acquired through use and disuse are inherited
It shows that different structures evolve for the same function
If humans could create new breeds in hundreds of years, nature could do the same over millions of years
questions.explanation:
Key idea: Darwin used artificial selection as evidence that selection can change a group of organisms a great deal.
By selective breeding, humans produced very different dog breeds in only a few hundred years.
If humans can do this so quickly, natural selection acting over millions of years could produce much larger changes, including new species.
Option (1) fails because all breeds still belong to the same species. Option (2) is Lamarck's idea, not this argument. Option (3) describes analogy.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Miller and other scientists ran experiments that simulated conditions on primitive earth. How many of the following were reported to form in these experiments?
Amino acids, sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments, fats, single-celled organisms
questions.explanation:
Miller obtained amino acids in his experiment.
NCERT says similar experiments by others formed sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments and fats.
That makes 5 substances.
Single-celled organisms were never produced in any such experiment. How the first self-replicating cell arose is still unknown.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are factual observations on which Darwin's natural selection is based?
(i) Natural resources are limited
(ii) Population sizes are stable except for seasonal fluctuations
(iii) Members of a population vary in characteristics, even though they look superficially similar
(iv) Most variations are inherited
(v) Characters acquired during the lifetime through use of organs are passed to offspring
(vi) The earth is about 4000 years old
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation:
(i) Correct: natural resources are limited.
(ii) Correct: population sizes stay stable apart from seasonal fluctuations.
(iii) Correct: members of a population vary, even if they look similar.
(iv) Correct: most variations are inherited.
(v) Incorrect: inheritance of characters acquired by use of organs is Lamarck's idea, not Darwin's.
(vi) Incorrect: a 4000-year-old earth belongs to special creation.
So four statements are factual observations behind natural selection.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Embryological similarities among vertebrate embryos, as proposed by Ernst Heckel, are no longer accepted as showing that an embryo passes through the adult stages of its ancestors.
Reason (R): Karl Ernst von Baer observed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: Haeckel's idea that embryos pass through the adult stages of their ancestors is no longer accepted.
R is true: von Baer observed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals.
R is the reason A was rejected, so R correctly explains A.
Note: the embryonic gill slits themselves are real. Only Haeckel's interpretation of them was disproved.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements is incorrect?
options: According to Darwin, fitness ultimately refers only to reproductive fitness
Lamarck explained the long neck of giraffes through the use of organs and the inheritance of acquired characters
According to deVries, mutations are small and directional, and evolution is gradual
Alfred Wallace, working in the Malay Archipelago, reached conclusions similar to Darwin's
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: Darwinian fitness ultimately means reproductive fitness.
(2) Correct: Lamarck explained the giraffe's long neck by use of organs and inheritance of acquired characters.
(3) Incorrect: deVries said mutations are large, random and directionless, and cause single-step speciation (saltation). Small, directional variation with gradual change was Darwin's view.
(4) Correct: Wallace, working in the Malay Archipelago, reached conclusions similar to Darwin's.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which feature of reptiles, absent in amphibians, helped them reproduce away from water?
options: Viviparity with the young protected inside the mother's body
Thick-shelled eggs that do not dry up in the sun
Stout and strong fins for moving on land
Eggs laid in jelly-coated masses in water
questions.explanation:
Reptiles lay thick-shelled eggs that do not dry up in the sun, unlike amphibian eggs. This freed them from depending on water for reproduction.
Viviparity is linked to mammals in this account, not to reptiles in general.
Stout, strong fins belong to lobefin fish.
Jelly-coated eggs laid in water are an amphibian feature.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When we observe stars in the night sky, we are in a way looking back in time.
Reason (R): Light reaching our eyes from a star began its journey millions of years ago from trillions of kilometres away.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
R is true. Stars are trillions of kilometres away, and their distances are measured in light years. The light reaching us left the star millions of years ago.
A is true. Because that light is so old, we see the star as it was in the past, so we are effectively looking back in time.
R directly explains why A holds.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: On the early earth, UV rays from the sun split water vapour into hydrogen and oxygen. What happened to the hydrogen so produced?
options: It combined with methane to form ammonia
Being lighter, H$_2$ escaped from the earth
It formed the ozone layer
It condensed to form the oceans
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: UV rays split water vapour into H$_2$ and O$_2$. Molecular hydrogen is very light, so it escaped from the earth's gravity.
Why not (3): it was oxygen that later contributed to the ozone layer.
Why not (1): oxygen, not hydrogen, reacted with ammonia and methane.
Why not (4): oceans formed from water vapour that fell as rain.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements is INCORRECT?
options: Homologous structures may perform quite different functions in different organisms
In divergent evolution, the same structure develops along different directions because of adaptation to different needs
Analogous structures arise when a structure inherited from a common ancestor is modified for the same function in the same habitat
Similarities in proteins and genes performing a given function point to the same shared ancestry as structural similarities do
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: homologous structures can do different jobs, e.g., a whale flipper and a bat wing.
(2) Correct: in divergent evolution, the same structure is modified in different directions to meet different needs.
(3) Incorrect: analogous structures are NOT inherited from a common ancestor. They are different structures in unrelated groups that evolve for the same function (convergent evolution). A modified structure inherited from a common ancestor describes homology.
(4) Correct: protein and gene similarities point to shared ancestry, just as structural similarities do.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Who disproved the embryological support for evolution proposed by Ernst Haeckel?
options: Charles Darwin
Hugo de Vries
Karl Ernst von Baer
Louis Pasteur
questions.explanation:
Ernst Haeckel proposed embryological support for evolution. He based it on features such as the vestigial gill slits seen in all vertebrate embryos.
Karl Ernst von Baer studied embryos carefully. He showed that embryos never pass through the adult stages of other animals, and this disproved Haeckel's proposal.
Darwin, de Vries and Pasteur are linked with natural selection, mutation theory and the refutation of spontaneous generation, respectively.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Analogous structures indicate that the organisms possessing them share a common ancestry.
Statement II: Analogous structures are not anatomically similar, although they perform similar functions.
Choose the correct option.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I is incorrect. Common ancestry is shown by homologous structures. Analogous structures arise by convergent evolution in unrelated groups, so they do not indicate a shared ancestor.
Statement II is correct. Analogous structures differ in anatomy but perform similar functions. Examples are the wings of a butterfly and a bird, or the eyes of an octopus and a mammal.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): When a section of a population migrates to another place and population, gene frequencies change in both the original and the new population.
Reason (R): Migrating individuals add new alleles to the population they join, and those alleles are lost from the population they leave.
Choose the correct option:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. When part of a population migrates into another population, gene frequencies change in both populations.
R is true. The new population gains the migrants' alleles, and the original population loses them.
R explains A, because this gain and loss is exactly why both frequencies change. Repeated migration of this kind is called gene flow.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): Flippers of penguins and dolphins are analogous structures.
Reason (R): A similar habitat results in the selection of similar adaptive features in different groups of organisms, directed toward the same function.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. Penguins (birds) and dolphins (mammals) are different groups, but both have flippers for swimming. The flippers are similar in function, not in origin, so they are analogous.
R is true. A similar aquatic habitat favoured similar adaptive features in both groups, all directed toward the same function of swimming. This is convergent evolution.
R explains why unrelated groups ended up with functionally similar flippers. That is exactly why the flippers are analogous.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are examples of evolution by anthropogenic action, as described in NCERT?
(i) Insects resistant to pesticides
(ii) Weeds resistant to herbicides
(iii) Bacteria resistant to antibiotics
(iv) Eukaryotic cells resistant to drugs used against them
(v) Variety of beaks in Darwin's finches
(vi) Diversification of marsupials in Australia
options: Two
Three
Four
Six
questions.explanation:
(i) Anthropogenic: pesticide-resistant insects are selected by human use of pesticides.
(ii) Anthropogenic: weeds become resistant to the herbicides humans apply.
(iii) Anthropogenic: bacteria become resistant to antibiotics humans use.
(iv) Anthropogenic: eukaryotic cells become resistant to drugs used against them.
(v) Not anthropogenic: Darwin's finches show natural adaptive radiation.
(vi) Not anthropogenic: Australian marsupials show natural adaptive radiation.
So four of the six are anthropogenic.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 revealed a stage of human evolution with a brain capacity of about 900 cc that probably ate meat. Which hominid was this?
options: Homo habilis
Australopithecus
Neanderthal man
Homo erectus
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: fossils found in Java in 1891 revealed Homo erectus, about 1.5 mya.
Homo erectus had a large brain of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. This matches every clue in the question.
The most tempting wrong option is Homo habilis. It had a smaller brain (650-800 cc) and probably did not eat meat.
Neanderthals (about 1400 cc) and Australopithecus do not match the Java find.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In England, collections made after industrialisation contained more dark-winged (melanised) moths than white-winged moths.
Reason (R): Industrial soot darkened the tree trunks and killed the light-coloured lichens, so dark moths were camouflaged from predators.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: after industrialisation, collections in England had more dark-winged moths than white-winged moths.
R is true: soot darkened tree trunks, and lichens, which cannot grow in polluted air, died.
Against the dark bark, predators easily picked off white moths, while dark moths stayed camouflaged and survived.
This natural selection explains the change in A, so R correctly explains A.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding the Hardy-Weinberg principle is incorrect?
options: The expression $p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ is the binomial expansion of $(p+q)^2$
When a drifted section of a population becomes so different that it forms a new species, the original drifted population acts as founders (founder effect)
Gene migration occurring repeatedly between populations results in gene flow
Genetic drift refers to change in allele frequency brought about by natural selection favouring the fittest
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: $(p+q)^2 = p^2 + 2pq + q^2 = 1$ is the binomial expansion behind Hardy-Weinberg.
(2) Correct: NCERT states that when a drifted sample becomes so different that it forms a new species, the original drifted population acts as founders. This is the founder effect.
(3) Correct: repeated gene migration between populations produces gene flow.
(4) Incorrect: genetic drift is a change in allele frequency that happens purely by chance. A change driven by selection favouring the fittest is natural selection, not drift.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to Darwin, the term 'fitness' of an individual or population ultimately refers only to its
options: physical strength and body size
reproductive fitness, that is, leaving more progeny
length of life span
ability to modify its organs through use
questions.explanation:
Darwin's fitness ultimately and only means reproductive fitness.
Those better fit in an environment leave more progeny than others and are therefore selected by nature.
Physical strength, body size or a long life span count only if they lead to more offspring. So options (1) and (3) fail.
Option (4), modifying organs through use, is Lamarck's idea, not Darwin's.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match the event in List-I with its approximate time in List-II.
List-I
A. First cellular forms of life appeared
B. Invertebrates were formed and active
C. Some land reptiles returned to water as fish-like reptiles (Ichthyosaurs)
D. Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared
List-II
I. 65 mya
II. 200 mya
III. 500 mya
IV. 2000 mya
options: A-IV, B-III, C-II, D-I
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-II, C-III, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
questions.explanation:
A. The first cellular forms appeared about 2000 mya, so A matches IV.
B. Invertebrates were formed and active about 500 mya, so B matches III.
C. Ichthyosaurs arose about 200 mya, so C matches II.
D. Dinosaurs disappeared about 65 mya, so D matches I.
Avoid swapping the 500 mya and 2000 mya dates.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements regarding 'evolution as a process versus a result' is correct as per NCERT?
options: When we describe the story of life on earth, evolution is treated as a process, and when we describe the story of the world, as a consequence of natural selection
When we describe the story of the world, evolution is described as a process, and when we describe the story of life on earth, as a consequence of natural selection
It is now clearly established that natural selection is only an end result and never a process
The world we see includes both successful and failed products of evolution in equal measure
questions.explanation:
Key NCERT fact: when we describe the story of this world, evolution is described as a process.
When we describe the story of life on earth, evolution is treated as a consequence of natural selection.
Option (2) matches this exactly. Option (1) is tempting but swaps the two cases.
Option (3) fails because NCERT says we are still not clear whether evolution and natural selection are processes or end results.
Option (4) fails because the world we see is mainly the successful stories of evolution, not failures in equal measure.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following pairs represents analogous organs?
options: Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
Forelimbs of whale and bat
Sweet potato and potato
Hearts of different vertebrates
questions.explanation:
Analogous organs have a different origin and structure but perform a similar function. They arise by convergent evolution.
Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem, yet both store food. They are therefore analogous, so option (3) fits.
Thorn and tendril, forelimbs of whale and bat, and vertebrate hearts each share a common origin. Their functions or forms differ, which makes them homologous and the result of divergent evolution.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A figure compares the skulls of an adult modern human, a baby chimpanzee and an adult chimpanzee. Which conclusion is correctly drawn from this comparison?
options: The adult chimpanzee skull resembles the adult human skull more than the baby chimpanzee skull does
The skulls of the baby and adult chimpanzee are nearly identical, and both differ greatly from the human skull
The baby chimpanzee skull is more like the adult human skull than the adult chimpanzee skull
The adult human skull resembles neither chimpanzee skull, which rules out a shared ancestry
questions.explanation:
NCERT compares the skulls of an adult human, a baby chimpanzee and an adult chimpanzee.
The baby chimpanzee skull is closer to the adult human skull than to the adult chimpanzee skull. The distinctly ape-like features, such as the projecting jaw and brow, develop as the chimpanzee grows.
Option (2) fails because baby and adult chimpanzee skulls differ noticeably.
Option (4) fails because the resemblance actually points to shared ancestry.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries put forward the idea of mutations in the first decade of the twentieth century. On which plant did he base this work?
options: Garden pea
Evening primrose
Snapdragon
Bougainvillea
questions.explanation:
deVries proposed that mutations drive evolution. He described mutations as large, sudden changes, which he called saltation.
He based this idea on his work on the evening primrose (Oenothera lamarckiana).
Garden pea is the tempting wrong option, but it belongs to Mendel's work on inheritance.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: In a population in Hardy–Weinberg equilibrium, 16% of individuals show the recessive phenotype (aa). What is the frequency of heterozygous (Aa) individuals?
questions.explanation:
Given: frequency of aa $= q^2 = 0.16$.
Formula: $p + q = 1$; heterozygote frequency $= 2pq$.
Substituting: $q = \sqrt{0.16} = 0.4$, so $p = 1 - 0.4 = 0.6$. Then $2pq = 2 \times 0.6 \times 0.4$.
So frequency of Aa $= 0.48$.
The trap options are 0.24 (forgetting the factor 2) and 0.36, which is $p^2$ (the AA frequency).
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following statements about the early earth are correct?
(i) The earth had a well-formed atmosphere right from the time of its formation.
(ii) UV radiation from the sun split water into hydrogen and oxygen.
(iii) The ozone layer was formed after oxygen became available on the early earth.
(iv) Oxygen combined with methane and ammonia to form water and CO$_2$.
(v) Life appeared about 500 million years before the formation of the earth.
questions.explanation:
(i) Incorrect: the early earth had no atmosphere at first.
(ii) Correct: UV rays split water into H$_2$ and O$_2$.
(iii) Correct: the ozone layer formed only after oxygen became available.
(iv) Correct: oxygen combined with CH$_4$ and NH$_3$ to form water and CO$_2$.
(v) Incorrect: life appeared 500 million years after the earth formed, not before.
So 3 statements are correct.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Consider two comparisons:
(1) The beaks of a seed-eating and an insectivorous Darwin's finch, both modified from the beak of a common ancestral finch.
(2) The overall body form of the Tasmanian wolf and the placental wolf, which belong to two separate radiations.
Which evolutionary patterns do comparisons (1) and (2) illustrate, respectively?
options: Convergent evolution; divergent evolution
Divergent evolution; convergent evolution
Divergent evolution in both
Convergent evolution in both
questions.explanation:
Comparison (1): the two finch beaks are modified from the same ancestral beak in different directions to suit different diets. A common structure diverging within one radiation is divergent evolution, and it gives homologous structures.
Comparison (2): the Tasmanian wolf and the placental wolf come from two separate radiations (marsupial and placental). They came to look alike because they occupy similar habitats. This is convergent evolution.
Option (1) reverses the two patterns, so it is wrong.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about the early earth, as described in NCERT, is INCORRECT?
options: Initially there was no atmosphere, and water vapour, $CH_4$, $CO_2$ and $NH_3$ released from the molten mass covered the surface.
UV rays from the sun split water into hydrogen and oxygen, and the lighter $H_2$ escaped.
Free oxygen released by the splitting of water built up as the main gas, so the atmosphere became oxidising before life appeared.
As the earth cooled, water vapour fell as rain and filled the depressions to form oceans.
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT says there was no atmosphere at first, and water vapour, $CH_4$, $CO_2$ and $NH_3$ released from the molten mass covered the surface.
(2) Correct: UV rays split water into $H_2$ and $O_2$, and the lighter $H_2$ escaped.
(3) Incorrect: the released oxygen did not build up as a free gas. It combined with $NH_3$ and $CH_4$ to form water, $CO_2$ and other compounds, so the early atmosphere stayed reducing.
(4) Correct: on cooling, water vapour fell as rain and filled depressions to form oceans.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils discovered in Java in 1891 belonged to a hominid that lived about 1.5 million years ago, had a brain capacity of about 900 cc and probably ate meat. Which hominid was this?
options: Homo habilis
Australopithecus
Homo erectus
Neanderthal man
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: fossils found in Java in 1891 belong to Homo erectus. It lived about 1.5 mya, had a brain of about 900 cc and probably ate meat.
The most tempting wrong option is Homo habilis. It had a smaller brain (650–800 cc) and probably did not eat meat.
Neanderthal man had a brain of about 1400 cc and lived much later.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the idea of 'panspermia', which some astronomers still favour, how did life arise on earth?
options: Living organisms arose from decaying straw and mud
Units of life called spores were transferred to earth from elsewhere in space
Organic molecules formed from inorganic constituents in the primitive oceans
All species were created in their present form about 4000 years ago
questions.explanation:
Panspermia proposes that spores, the units of life, were transferred to different planets, including earth, from outer space.
Option (1) describes spontaneous generation.
Option (3) describes chemical evolution (Oparin–Haldane).
Option (4) describes special creation.
Only option (2) matches panspermia.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Darwin observed many varieties of small black birds, later called Darwin's finches, during his voyage. Where did he observe them?
options: Malay Archipelago
Galapagos Islands
Australian mainland
Madagascar
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: during his voyage, Darwin visited the Galapagos Islands. There he saw many varieties of small black birds, later called Darwin's finches.
He proposed that all these varieties had evolved on the island itself, which is an example of adaptive radiation.
The tempting option, the Malay Archipelago, is linked with Alfred Wallace, who reached similar conclusions about natural selection. It is not where the finches were seen.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
B. Sweet potato and potato
C. Different breeds of dogs
D. Similar proteins and genes performing a given function in diverse organisms
List-II
I. Biochemical evidence of shared ancestry
II. Analogy in plants
III. Homology in plants
IV. Artificial selection by man
Choose the correct answer.
options: A-III, B-II, C-IV, D-I
A-II, B-III, C-IV, D-I
A-III, B-II, C-I, D-IV
A-II, B-III, C-I, D-IV
questions.explanation:
A: The Bougainvillea thorn and the Cucurbita tendril are both modified from the same structure (stem/axillary bud). They are homologous: A-III.
B: Sweet potato is a root and potato is a stem, yet both store food. They are analogous: B-II.
C: Dog breeds were produced by human breeding, which is artificial selection: C-IV.
D: Similar proteins and genes across diverse organisms are biochemical evidence of common ancestry: D-I.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which one of the following statements about dinosaurs and early mammals is INCORRECT according to NCERT?
options: Tyrannosaurus rex, the biggest dinosaur, was about 20 feet tall and had huge dagger-like teeth
NCERT concludes that dinosaurs were wiped out about 65 mya solely because of climatic changes
The first mammals were shrew-like, and their fossils are small in size
Early mammals were viviparous and better at sensing and avoiding danger than reptiles
questions.explanation:
(1) Correct: NCERT describes Tyrannosaurus rex as the biggest dinosaur, about 20 feet tall, with dagger-like teeth.
(2) Incorrect: NCERT says the true reason for dinosaur extinction is not known. Some suggest climatic change, others suggest most dinosaurs evolved into birds, and the truth may lie in between. 'Solely climatic change' misstates NCERT.
(3) Correct: the first mammals were shrew-like, with small fossils.
(4) Correct: early mammals were viviparous and better at sensing and avoiding danger.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: According to the Hardy–Weinberg principle, what is the term for the total genes and their alleles in a population remaining constant from generation to generation?
options: Gene flow
Genetic drift
Genetic equilibrium
Founder effect
questions.explanation:
Hardy–Weinberg principle: in a population, allele frequencies stay stable and are constant from generation to generation.
When the gene pool (total genes and their alleles) stays constant like this, the population is in genetic equilibrium.
Gene flow, genetic drift and the founder effect are all processes that change allele frequencies. They disturb equilibrium rather than describe it.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Embryos of all vertebrates develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head. In which group of adult vertebrates are these gill slits functional organs?
options: Amphibians
Reptiles
Mammals
Fishes
questions.explanation:
All vertebrate embryos, including the human embryo, develop a row of vestigial gill slits just behind the head.
These slits are functional organs only in adult fish.
Amphibians are the tempting choice because their larvae have gills. However, NCERT states that gill slits are not found in any other adult vertebrate, so amphibians do not fit.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The idea of 'Panspermia', still favoured by some astronomers, proposes that:
options: units of life called spores were transferred to different planets, including earth
life arose spontaneously from rotting and decaying matter
all living species were created as such and have remained unchanged
life arose on earth through chemical evolution in a reducing atmosphere
questions.explanation:
Panspermia is an idea traced to early Greek thinkers and still favoured by some astronomers. It holds that units of life called spores were transferred to different planets, including earth.
Option (2) describes spontaneous generation.
Option (3) describes special creation.
Option (4) is the Oparin–Haldane chemical evolution view.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following statements about industrial melanism in moths in England is correct?
options: In rural areas without industrialisation, melanic moths outnumbered white-winged moths
Lichens grew abundantly on tree trunks in polluted areas
After industrialisation, white-winged moths were completely wiped out
Predators readily spot a moth that contrasts with its background
questions.explanation:
(1) Incorrect: in rural, unpolluted areas the white-winged moths remained more numerous.
(2) Incorrect: lichens do not grow in polluted areas. They are pollution indicators, so polluted bark became dark and bare.
(3) Incorrect: selection shifts frequencies. White moths became fewer but were not wiped out completely.
(4) Correct: predators easily spot a moth that contrasts with its background. Camouflaged moths therefore survive and increase in number.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Analogous organs arise due to:
options: divergent evolution
artificial selection
genetic drift
convergent evolution
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Analogous organs perform similar functions but differ in structure and origin. Examples are the wings of a butterfly and a bird, and the eyes of an octopus and a mammal.
They arise when unrelated groups adapt to similar needs or habitats. This is convergent evolution.
Divergent evolution is the tempting wrong option, but it produces homologous organs from a common ancestor.
Genetic drift and artificial selection do not explain analogy.
Answer: (4)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q6)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Fossils are generally found in:
options: Sedimentary rocks
Igneous rocks
Metamorphic rocks
Any type of rock
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Fossils form when dead organisms are buried in layers of sediment. These layers slowly harden into sedimentary rock.
Igneous rocks form from molten magma, and metamorphic rocks form under intense heat and pressure. Both processes destroy organic remains.
So fossils are found mainly in sedimentary rocks, and option (4), 'any type of rock', is wrong.
Answer: (1)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q11)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II:
List-I
(A) Australopithecines
(B) Homo habilis
(C) Homo erectus
(D) Neanderthal man
List-II
(I) Brain capacity 650–800 cc; probably did not eat meat
(II) Brain capacity about 1400 cc; lived in near east and central Asia
(III) Hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit
(IV) Brain capacity about 900 cc; probably ate meat
Choose the correct answer:
options: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II
A-I, B-III, C-IV, D-II
A-III, B-IV, C-I, D-II
A-IV, B-I, C-III, D-II
questions.explanation:
A–III: Australopithecines lived in East African grasslands; they hunted with stone weapons but essentially ate fruit.
B–I: Homo habilis had a brain capacity of 650–800 cc and probably did not eat meat.
C–IV: Homo erectus had about 900 cc and probably ate meat.
D–II: Neanderthal man had about 1400 cc and lived in the near east and central Asia.
The common trap is swapping the diets of H. habilis and H. erectus.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following were reported to form in Miller's experiment or in similar later experiments simulating early-earth conditions?
Amino acids, sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments, fats, membrane-bound cells, self-replicating bacteria
questions.explanation:
Miller's experiment produced amino acids.
Similar later experiments produced sugars, nitrogen bases, pigments and fats.
That gives 5 items in total.
No membrane-bound cells or self-replicating bacteria formed in any of these experiments. They supported only chemical evolution, not the origin of living cells.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Appearance of antibiotic-resistant bacteria is an example of:
options: adaptive radiation
transduction
pre-existing variation in the population
divergent evolution
questions.explanation:
Key fact: In a bacterial population, a few individuals already carry resistance genes before the antibiotic is used.
The antibiotic kills the susceptible bacteria. The resistant variants survive and multiply, so resistance spreads.
This is selection acting on pre-existing variation, as NCERT notes for herbicide and pesticide resistance too.
Adaptive radiation is tempting, but it refers to divergence of one ancestral group into many forms in different habitats, like Darwin's finches. It does not describe resistance arising within one population.
Answer: (3)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q8)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I
A. Homo habilis
B. Homo erectus
C. Neanderthal man
D. Dryopithecus
List-II
I. Fossils found in Java in 1891; brain about 900 cc
II. Brain capacity 650-800 cc; probably did not eat meat
III. More ape-like primate existing about 15 mya
IV. Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
options: A-I, B-II, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III
A-II, B-I, C-III, D-IV
A-IV, B-II, C-I, D-III
questions.explanation:
A. Homo habilis: brain 650-800 cc, probably did not eat meat → II.
B. Homo erectus: Java fossils of 1891, brain about 900 cc → I.
C. Neanderthal man: brain about 1400 cc, buried their dead → IV.
D. Dryopithecus: more ape-like primate of about 15 mya → III.
The correct match is A-II, B-I, C-IV, D-III.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Hugo deVries proposed the idea of mutation as the cause of evolution. On which organism was his work based?
options: Garden pea
Evening primrose
Snapdragon
Fruit fly
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: Hugo deVries proposed mutation as the cause of evolution. His idea came from work on evening primrose in the early twentieth century.
He observed sudden large variations in this plant and called them mutations.
Garden pea is the tempting option, but it was Mendel's experimental plant for the laws of inheritance.
The fruit fly was Morgan's organism for linkage studies.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following pairs are homologous?
1. Forelimbs of whale and bat
2. Heart of a frog and heart of a human
3. Thorn of Bougainvillea and tendril of Cucurbita
4. Wings of butterfly and bird
5. Flippers of penguin and dolphin
6. Sweet potato and potato
7. Brain of a fish and brain of a human
options: Three
Four
Five
Two
questions.explanation:
1. Whale and bat forelimbs: homologous, since both are mammalian forelimbs with the same bone plan.
2. Frog and human hearts: homologous, as vertebrate hearts.
3. Bougainvillea thorn and Cucurbita tendril: homologous, with the same origin but different functions.
4. Butterfly and bird wings: analogous.
5. Penguin and dolphin flippers: analogous.
6. Sweet potato (root) and potato (stem): analogous.
7. Fish and human brains: homologous, as vertebrate brains.
That makes four homologous pairs (1, 2, 3, 7).
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is NOT one of the three connotations of the theory of special creation?
options: All living organisms seen today were created as such
The diversity was always the same since creation and will remain the same in future
The earth is about 4000 years old
The earth is billions of years old and life forms have changed gradually
questions.explanation:
The theory of special creation has three connotations:
(a) All living organisms were created as such.
(b) Diversity has always been the same and will stay the same.
(c) The earth is about 4000 years old.
Options (1), (2) and (3) are these three ideas. Option (4), an earth billions of years old with gradually changing life, is the evidence-based view that challenged special creation. It is not part of the theory.
Answer: (4)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: A graph shows the number of individuals plotted against the value of a heritable trait. Before selection, the curve is bell-shaped with a single peak at the mean. After many generations, the number of individuals near the mean has fallen, and two peaks have appeared at both ends of the distribution. Which type of natural selection does this represent?
options: Stabilising selection
Directional selection
Disruptive selection
Genetic drift
questions.explanation:
Disruptive selection favours individuals at both extremes of the trait. Individuals near the mean become fewer, and two peaks form at the ends.
This matches the graph described in the question.
Stabilising selection would make the single peak taller and narrower at the mean.
Directional selection would move the single peak towards one end.
Genetic drift is a random change in allele frequency, not a type of natural selection.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Sweet potato and potato are cited as an example of analogy because
options: both are modified roots that store food
both are modified stems that store food
sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem, yet both store food
sweet potato is a modified stem and potato is a modified root, and they perform different functions
questions.explanation:
Analogous organs differ in origin and structure but perform the same function.
Sweet potato is a modified root and potato is a modified stem (tuber). Both store food, so they are analogous.
Options (1) and (2) make them the same in origin, which would mean homology, not analogy. Option (4) swaps root and stem and wrongly says their functions differ.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The placental wolf and the Tasmanian wolf look similar even though one is a placental mammal and the other a marsupial.
Reason (R): Their similarity is due to divergent evolution of the same structure from a recent common ancestor.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true: the placental wolf and the Tasmanian (marsupial) wolf look alike.
R is false: their similarity is not due to divergent evolution from a recent common ancestor.
The placental and marsupial lineages evolved separately. Each produced similar forms through convergent evolution, an example of adaptive radiation in parallel.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: According to deVries, mutation caused speciation in a single large step, which he called saltation.
Statement II: For Darwin, evolution was a gradual process based on small heritable variations.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
questions.explanation:
Statement I: Correct. Hugo deVries studied mutations in evening primrose. He proposed that a single-step large mutation causes speciation and called this saltation.
Statement II: Correct. Darwin saw evolution as gradual. It works through small, directional heritable variations that natural selection accumulates over many generations.
The two views differ: deVries said mutations are large and random, while Darwin's variations are small and directional. Even so, each statement correctly describes its own author's view.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Bacteria resistant to antibiotics and pests resistant to pesticides now appear within months or years rather than centuries. NCERT describes this kind of evolution as
options: Evolution by anthropogenic action
Saltation caused by a single large mutation
Adaptive radiation from an ancestral stock
Evolution by use and disuse of organs
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: excessive use of herbicides, pesticides and antibiotics has selected resistant varieties of pests and microbes within months or years. NCERT calls this evolution by anthropogenic (human-caused) action.
This is natural selection working on a short time scale, with humans changing the environment.
Saltation is a single large mutation causing a big jump, as in de Vries' idea. Adaptive radiation is divergence from one ancestor into many habitats. Use and disuse is Lamarck's theory. None of these describes resistance selected by human chemicals.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Match List-I with List-II.
List-I:
(A) Homo habilis
(B) Homo erectus
(C) Neanderthal man
(D) Ramapithecus
List-II:
(i) Brain about 1400 cc; buried their dead
(ii) Brain 650-800 cc; probably did not eat meat
(iii) Brain about 900 cc; probably ate meat
(iv) Man-like primate existing about 15 mya
Choose the correct option.
options: A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(iii), B-(ii), C-(i), D-(iv)
A-(ii), B-(i), C-(iii), D-(iv)
A-(iv), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(ii)
questions.explanation:
A, Homo habilis: brain 650-800 cc, probably did not eat meat, so (ii).
B, Homo erectus: brain about 900 cc, probably ate meat, so (iii).
C, Neanderthal man: brain about 1400 cc, buried their dead, so (i).
D, Ramapithecus: the more man-like primate of about 15 mya, so (iv).
The matching is A-(ii), B-(iii), C-(i), D-(iv).
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following are mammals that live wholly in water, as mentioned in NCERT?
Whales, Ichthyosaurs, Dolphins, Coelacanth, Seals, Sea cows
questions.explanation:
NCERT gives whales, dolphins, seals and sea cows as examples of mammals that live wholly in water.
Ichthyosaurs were fish-like reptiles, not mammals.
The Coelacanth is a lobefin fish.
So the count is 4.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
How many of the following can disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium in a population?
Gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination, natural selection, random mating, large population size
options: Three
Four
Five
Six
questions.explanation:
NCERT names five factors that change allele frequencies: gene flow, genetic drift, mutation, genetic recombination and natural selection. All five disturb Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium.
Random mating and a large population size are conditions the equilibrium needs. They help maintain it rather than disturb it.
So five of the listed items disturb the equilibrium.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: The earth, a member of the solar system of the Milky Way galaxy, is believed to have been formed about:
options: 13.8 billion years ago
2000 million years ago
4.5 billion years ago
3 billion years ago
questions.explanation:
NCERT fact: the earth, part of the solar system in the Milky Way galaxy, formed about 4.5 billion years ago.
Why not (1): 13.8 billion years is the approximate age of the universe, not the earth.
Why not (2): about 2000 million years ago is when the first cellular life forms appeared.
Why not (4): 3 billion years does not match the NCERT figure.
Answer: (3)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Arrange the following events in the correct chronological order, from oldest to most recent:
(A) Fish-like reptiles such as Ichthyosaurs evolved
(B) Invertebrates were formed and active
(C) First cellular forms of life appeared
(D) Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared
(E) Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed
options: C, B, A, D, E
C, A, B, D, E
B, C, A, E, D
C, B, D, A, E
questions.explanation:
Use the NCERT timeline:
(C) First cellular forms of life appeared about 2000 mya, so this is the oldest event.
(B) Invertebrates were formed and active by about 500 mya.
(A) Fish-like reptiles such as Ichthyosaurs evolved about 200 mya.
(D) Dinosaurs suddenly disappeared about 65 mya. Option (4) wrongly places this before the Ichthyosaurs.
(E) Dryopithecus and Ramapithecus existed about 15 mya, so this is the most recent.
The order is C → B → A → D → E.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Statement I: Ichthyosaurs were fish-like reptiles that evolved, probably around 200 mya, from land reptiles that went back into water.
Statement II: Specimens of the first amphibians that evolved from lobefins are still alive today in the form of frogs and salamanders.
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
questions.explanation:
Statement I is correct. Some land reptiles went back into water, probably around 200 mya, and evolved into fish-like reptiles called Ichthyosaurs.
Statement II is incorrect. The first amphibians were the ancestors of modern frogs and salamanders, but NCERT says no specimens of them are left.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: During the age of reptiles, which plants slowly fell and formed coal deposits?
options: Giant ferns (pteridophytes)
Seaweeds
Flowering plants (angiosperms)
Mosses (bryophytes)
questions.explanation:
NCERT states that giant ferns (pteridophytes) were present during reptilian dominance. They slowly fell and formed coal deposits.
Seaweeds were early aquatic forms, not coal-forming land plants.
Mosses were never giant forest plants.
Angiosperms arose later.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question:
Assertion (A): In England, collections made in 1920 showed more dark-winged (melanised) moths than white-winged moths, reversing the proportion seen in the 1850s.
Reason (R): Industrial soot darkened tree trunks and the whitish lichens disappeared, so dark moths were camouflaged from predators while white moths were easily spotted.
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
questions.explanation:
A is true. In 1850s England, white-winged moths outnumbered dark ones. Collections made in 1920 showed more melanised moths, so the proportion had reversed.
R is true. Industrial smoke and soot darkened tree trunks and killed the whitish lichens. Dark moths were then camouflaged, while white moths stood out and were picked off by predators.
R explains A because this selective predation is what raised the proportion of dark moths. It is a classic case of natural selection. Neither form was completely eliminated.
Answer: (1)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Alfred Wallace reached conclusions similar to Darwin's on natural selection at around the same time. Where did Wallace carry out his work as a naturalist?
options: Galapagos Islands
Malay Archipelago
Australian island continent
East African grasslands
questions.explanation:
Alfred Wallace was a naturalist who worked in the Malay Archipelago. He independently reached conclusions similar to Darwin's on natural selection at around the same time.
The Galapagos Islands are the tempting wrong option. They are linked with Darwin's observations of finches, not with Wallace.
Answer: (2)

questions.subject: Biology
questions.question: Which of the following is used as an atmospheric pollution indicator?
options: Lepidoptera
Lichens
Lycopersicon
Lycopodium
questions.explanation:
Key fact: Lichens are very sensitive to air pollutants, especially sulphur dioxide (SO$_2$), and do not grow in polluted areas.
So their presence means clean air and their absence means polluted air. This makes them atmospheric pollution indicators.
Lepidoptera (moths) is the tempting option because of industrial melanism. Moth colour, however, changed only indirectly, through soot-darkened bark and the loss of lichens. The moths themselves are not the standard pollution indicator.
Lycopersicon (tomato) and Lycopodium (a club moss) have no such role.
Answer: (2)
questions.credit: Source: NCERT Exemplar Biology Class 12, Ch 7 (MCQ Q1)

questions.subject: Biology
